speaker: Narrator
text: Welcome to Willowbrook, a quiet village of gardens and friendly neighbours. You are the village detective, and everyone knows you are good at finding things.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Hello! I'm Marmalade. I will help you. Use the arrow buttons to move, and press OK to choose.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Let's practise. Can you find your reading glasses?

speaker: Marmalade
text: Your reading glasses have two round lenses.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Well done! Now, some news. The lantern for tonight's autumn fair has gone dim. Three little light charms have rolled away around the village.

speaker: Narrator
text: You are ready to begin. Let's visit the bakery first.

speaker: Narrator
text: Well done, detective! You finished Welcome to Willowbrook.

speaker: Narrator
text: What do you like to do on a quiet morning?

speaker: Narrator

text: Chapter 1. The Bakery. Help Mrs. Bramble at the bakery and find the first light charm.

speaker: Narrator
text: Welcome back! Last time: You were at the bakery, helping Mrs. Bramble look for the first light charm. Let's carry on.

text: Welcome back! Last time you finished The Bakery. Let's carry on.

speaker: Narrator
text: The lantern for tonight's autumn fair has gone dim. We are finding three little light charms to make it shine again. Right now: Help Mrs. Bramble at the bakery and find the first light charm.

speaker: Narrator
text: The bakery smells of warm bread. Mrs. Bramble is busy baking for the fair.

speaker: Mrs. Bramble
text: Good morning, detective! I was baking a pear tart for the fair when a little light charm rolled off my table. Could you help me tidy up first?

speaker: Marmalade
text: Find the honey pot, the loaf of bread and the strawberries.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The honey pot is golden and round.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The loaf of bread is brown and crusty.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The strawberries are small and red.

speaker: Mrs. Bramble
text: Thank you, that's much tidier! My recipe cards are all mixed up. Each card has a twin. Could you put the pairs together?

speaker: Marmalade
text: Find two cards that are the same.

speaker: Mrs. Bramble
text: Lovely, all in pairs again! Now, a little question before we look for the charm.

speaker: Marmalade
text: What fruit was Mrs. Bramble using in her tart?

speaker: Marmalade
text: She told you when you arrived. It is a sweet green fruit.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Look! Something is twinkling under the last recipe card. It's the first light charm!

speaker: Narrator
text: You found the first light charm! Mrs. Bramble gives you a warm scone to say thank you. Two more charms to find.

speaker: Narrator
text: Well done, detective! You finished The Bakery.

speaker: Narrator
text: Did you ever bake bread or cakes? What did you like to make?

speaker: Narrator
text: What was your favourite treat when you were young?

speaker: Narrator
text: Which smells remind you of a warm kitchen?

speaker: Narrator
text: Chapter 2. The Garden. Help Mr. Hollis in his garden and find the second light charm.

speaker: Narrator
text: Welcome back! Last time: You were in Mr. Hollis's garden, looking for the second light charm. Let's carry on.

speaker: Narrator
text: Welcome back! Last time you finished The Garden. Let's carry on.

speaker: Narrator
text: The lantern for tonight's autumn fair has gone dim. We are finding three little light charms to make it shine again. Right now: Help Mr. Hollis in his garden and find the second light charm.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Hollis's garden is bright with autumn colours. He is raking leaves into a tidy pile.

speaker: Mr. Hollis
text: Hello, detective! I saw something sparkle near the flower beds, but my eyes aren't what they were. Shall we look together?

speaker: Marmalade
text: Find the ladybird, the mushroom and the chestnut.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The ladybird is small and red with black spots.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The mushroom has a round cap and a little stalk.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The chestnut is shiny and brown.

speaker: Mr. Hollis
text: Thank you! Oh dear, my basket is all muddled. Some things belong in the garden, and some belong in the kitchen.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Put each thing where it belongs.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The sparkle is under the sleeping flowers. I know a kind spell to wake them for a moment. Watch, then do the same!

speaker: Marmalade
text: Watch the magic, then press the same symbols in the same order.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The flowers are opening! And look, there between the petals is the second light charm!

speaker: Mr. Hollis
text: Before you go, here is a riddle my grandmother used to tell me.

speaker: Marmalade
text: I am tall and yellow, and I turn my face to the sun. What am I?

speaker: Marmalade
text: Think of a big, bright yellow flower.

speaker: Narrator
text: You found the second light charm! Mr. Hollis gives you a bunch of autumn flowers. Just one more charm to find.

speaker: Narrator
text: Well done, detective! You finished The Garden.

speaker: Narrator
text: Did you ever have a garden? What did you like to grow?

speaker: Narrator
text: What is your favourite flower?

speaker: Narrator
text: Which season do you like best, and why?

speaker: Narrator
text: Chapter 3. The Library. Help Miss Penrose at the library and find the third light charm.

speaker: Narrator
text: Welcome back! Last time: You were at the library, helping Miss Penrose look for the third light charm. Let's carry on.

speaker: Narrator
text: Welcome back! Last time you finished The Library. Let's carry on.

speaker: Narrator
text: The lantern for tonight's autumn fair has gone dim. We are finding three little light charms to make it shine again. Right now: Help Miss Penrose at the library and find the third light charm.

speaker: Narrator
text: The village library is quiet and warm. Tall shelves are full of books, and a clock ticks softly.

speaker: Miss Penrose
text: Welcome, detective! I was reading a lovely book about the sea when I heard a little tinkle. I think the last charm has rolled somewhere in here.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Find the magnifying glass, the candle and the key.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The magnifying glass has a round glass and a handle.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The candle is tall, with a little flame on top.

speaker: Marmalade
text: The key is small and golden.

speaker: Miss Penrose
text: Thank you! People leave all sorts of things here. Books and papers go on the bookshelf, and hats and umbrellas go to the cloakroom.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Put each thing where it belongs.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Something glints behind the reading cards. Let's put the pairs together and look underneath!

speaker: Marmalade
text: Find two cards that are the same.

speaker: Miss Penrose
text: Lovely work! Before you look, a little question for a good detective.

speaker: Marmalade
text: What was Miss Penrose's book about?

speaker: Marmalade
text: She told you when you arrived. Think of waves and boats.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Look under the last card! It's the third light charm, shining brightly!

speaker: Narrator
text: You found the third light charm! Miss Penrose claps her hands. Now let's take all three charms to the village square.

speaker: Narrator
text: Well done, detective! You finished The Library.

speaker: Narrator
text: What kind of books or stories do you enjoy?

speaker: Narrator
text: Did you have a favourite place to sit and read?

speaker: Narrator
text: Is there a song or a poem you like?

speaker: Narrator
text: Chapter 4. The Lantern Lights Up. Bring the three light charms to the lantern and light it for the fair.

speaker: Narrator
text: Welcome back! Last time: You were in the village square, getting ready to light the lantern. Let's carry on.

speaker: Narrator
text: Welcome back! Last time you finished The Lantern Lights Up. Let's carry on.

speaker: Narrator
text: The lantern for tonight's autumn fair has gone dim. We are finding three little light charms to make it shine again. Right now: Bring the three light charms to the lantern and light it for the fair.

speaker: Narrator
text: The village square is ready for the fair. There is bunting, a band, and a big lantern in the middle. Everyone has come to watch.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Here are the three light charms you found. Before we light the lantern, let's thank the friends who helped us.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Who was baking a pear tart?

speaker: Marmalade
text: It was at the bakery, where the bread smelled so good.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Who was raking leaves in the garden?

speaker: Marmalade
text: He looks after the flower beds.

speaker: Marmalade
text: Now for the kindest spell of all. Watch the magic, then do the same, and the lantern will shine!

speaker: Marmalade
text: Watch the magic, then press the same symbols in the same order.

speaker: Narrator
text: The three charms glow, and the great lantern lights up with a warm golden light! Everyone cheers, and the band begins to play.

speaker: Mrs. Bramble
text: Thank you, detective! The fair can begin. Willowbrook is lucky to have you.

speaker: Narrator
text: You solved the mystery of the lantern! Enjoy the autumn fair, detective.

speaker: Narrator
text: Well done, detective! You finished The Lantern Lights Up.

speaker: Narrator
text: Did you ever go to a fair or a street party? What was it like?

speaker: Narrator
text: What music do you like to sing or dance to?

speaker: Narrator
text: What makes a celebration special for you?

speaker: Narrator
text: You solved The Lantern of Willowbrook! You can play any chapter again from Case files.
